description: Inverts the polarity (phase) of a sound: every sample is negated. Verified SAMPLE-EXACT: output == -input with zero residual (max |out + in| = 0.0) on mono and stereo (both channels inverted); duration static and exact at 1 s and 2 s. Takes NO parameters. Deterministic (identical decoded shas 1.2 s apart). Sibling mode 2 (stereo enhancement) is curated separately; it is stereo-only, while this mode accepts any channel count.
musical_use: The cancellation scalpel. Mix an inverted copy against the original and they null to silence - so invert-and-mix isolates WHAT A PROCESS CHANGED: run a sound through any transform (e.g. distort fractal), invert the dry original, submix the two, and only the added/altered component survives (SoundThread ships exactly this recipe). Same trick extracts a stereo file's side content or checks whether two takes are really identical. Also plain mixing hygiene: flip a layer that partially cancels against another (kick + sub-bass) to turn destructive interference constructive - inaudible alone, decisive in a sum. Note the null only works while both copies stay sample-aligned: any time-shift, resample or lossy step between them breaks the cancellation. Inversion itself is inaudible in isolation; it only matters in combination.

examples.description: Invert a processed layer to isolate the processing residue.
examples.expected_use: Invert the DRY original, then submix mix it at equal level and time 0 against the processed version: the shared component nulls, leaving only what the process added.

known_issues: Pure sample negation, verified exact (out == -in, max residual 0.0; stereo inverts both channels). No parameters, no options.

Cancellation workflows require sample alignment and identical levels - the engine's 16-bit CDP pipeline preserves this for CDP-to-CDP chains, but any resampling or level change between the copies breaks the null.

Duration static and sample-exact (1 s and 2 s verified). Deterministic (identical decoded shas 1.2 s apart). Mono and stereo accepted; mode 2 of this program is stereo-only and curated as a separate entry.
